rationale: The edit wraps JSON.parse of stored audit details and each presigned-URL signing call in bare `catch (e) {}` blocks inside a service; a malformed details blob or a failing signing call is dropped and the caller gets audits that look intact.

The added try/catch only enriches an optional `port` field; a relative or bare host does not parse as a URL by contract, and the documented result shape treats port as optional, so the fallback is the intended absence, not a hidden fault.
New `snapshotLayout` catches every error, logs it and returns null, so a failed layout fetch is indistinguishable from a layout with no fields and the publish UI continues as if it succeeded.

The SDK migration keeps the previous behavior of logging the S3 get error and returning null, and the in-scope caller `getFileHandle` turns that null into a rejected promise, so no new failure is hidden by the edit.

`uploadFromUrl` already logged and returned undefined on failure, and the edit widens the hiding: the new `!res.ok` throw is immediately caught and swallowed by the same catch, and a zero content-length response returns undefined with no log at all.

The edit turns the abstract `uploadFromUrl` into a concrete method whose catch logs and returns undefined, which is also the normal return for a URL that needs no upload, so a failed fetch or upload leaves the caller unable to tell the file was never stored.

Malformed attachment JSON and unparsable old data used to raise the field validation error, and the edit swallows both into an empty array and an empty map, so a corrupt payload is saved as if the cell were simply empty.

New `patchUrl` only decorates an outgoing link with user query params and returns the caller's own url unchanged when it does not parse, so nothing that matters to correctness is hidden; the URL still navigates.

The added try/catch blocks cover a best-effort telemetry buffer in localStorage (read failure yields an empty list, write failure drops the events), which the rule names as best-effort side work; the comment states the events are lost as before.

The edit only routes localStorage access through small accessors that return null when storage is unavailable in an embedded webview, which is the documented absent-value contract for an optional redirect hint, not a failure of an operation that matters.

New `parseJson` is a documented try-parse helper whose contract says an absent or unparseable value yields the caller's fallback, so the catch inside it is the expected-absence exception rather than a swallowed fault.

When the plan text does not parse, `parseExplainPlanValue` yields an empty plan but `parseExplainExecution` keeps the original text as `raw` and shows it, so the user sees the unparsed plan instead of a fault being hidden; a truly empty result still throws.

New `safeGroup` catches every list-request failure and returns `{ items: [], total: 0 }`, so a network or permission failure on teams, topics, platforms, webhooks or firewall rules is reported as a project that simply has none.

The added catches are boolean probes that fall back to the fail-safe answer (not installed, stub stale) and the patched CLI entry handler that ignores only the documented `process.exit` throw while logging anything else; the promise it is attached to is nobody's to await, which the rule puts out of scope.

The new fetch of a site-origin cover image returns null on a non-ok response or a failed fetch, which is the same value a caller already gets for 'no image', so a decorative asset is skipped and the cover still renders.

New `parseDedicatedConnectionString` swallows a URL parse failure and returns an empty database name plus `ssl: true`, so a malformed connection string is presented as valid credentials with a substituted database name instead of a failure the caller can see.

The added catch and metadata probe both fail to the conservative branch (return null keeps every command on the deep copy path, unknown metadata returns true), so nothing that mattered is silently skipped; the fallback is the safe default.

`findRegExp` now catches an invalid search pattern and falls back to `RegExp("")`, so a bad regex the user typed produces an empty result list instead of surfacing the error; an empty result is exactly how 'no matches' looks.
The edit only adds a display conversion for object or array cell values and reuses the existing `?? ""` display fallback; no failure path is caught or converted.

Both new helpers are documented display formatters that fall back to the currency code when the code or locale is invalid or `formatToParts` is missing, so the fallback is the documented output contract, not a hidden fault in required data.

The new `consoleVariablesQueryOptions(...).catch(() => {})` in the prefetch batch lets a cache-warming fetch fail without failing the loader; the component's own query still fetches and reports its error, so no failure is hidden from anyone who can act on it.

The edit moves the non-critical invoice banner prefetch into the background with `.catch(() => {})`; it is cache warming for a query marked skipInitialLoader, so its failure only means the consumer fetches it again and shows its own error.
Both new catches only restore the watcher and rethrow, so the error still reaches the request handler and the caller; the failure is not converted into a normal result.

The edit keeps the existing per-link skip but reports it through the capped warning reporter plus a final skipped-links summary, and the newly skipped aborted-transaction case is counted and warned about, so the failure now reaches the operator instead of being hidden.
The new `tracked` wrapper only adds an analytics event and rethrows the original error; the registration catch that logs instead of throwing was already there before the edit.
The new catch converts a failed SDK call into a typed `GrowthError` classification (rate limit, server error, message) and rethrows it, so the caller still receives a failure it must handle.

Every new catch matches one specific expected error (duplicate key across the three dialects) and rethrows anything else, and the batch insert replaces the per-row catches with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, which is idempotent rather than swallowing.

The new catch around the driver requires is narrow: it only falls back to the cwd node_modules copy on MODULE_NOT_FOUND and rethrows any other loader error, and an unknown name still throws TypeError.

Both branches catch every error with a bare `catch {}` (create index, drop index) on the assumption it was an already-exists error, so a permission or invalid-schema failure lets the migration record as applied while the index is missing, and a rollback silently leaves it behind.
The edit only updates route path patterns for the newer router syntax; the two catches that treat a 404 as expected and rethrow anything else are unchanged.

The remaining catches cover a best-effort screen wake lock whose failure only means the screen may sleep; the release failure was already ignored before the edit, so correct operation never depends on it.

The added `.catch(() => {})` covers releasing a short-TTL cache claim in a finally after the account already exists, which cannot change correctness because the TTL expires the key anyway; the comment states the accounted reason.

The new catch around `removeLabel` swallows every error with no code check, then the step logs and posts that the label was removed, so a permission or API failure leaves the invalid label on the issue while the action reports success.
The edit only adds a fire-and-forget `loadAppInfo()` call after sign-in, and that function already sets a visible error status and logs on failure; no failure is converted into a normal result.
The new catch records a visible error state for the cell and rethrows, so the failure still reaches the caller; the only log-only catch in the file is the pre-existing button-action one, unchanged.
The widened catch now also logs the error and still turns the failure into a visible outcome (redirect to the auth-error notice) at the request boundary, which the rule exempts.

The failure was silent before (an unhandled rejection in the interval) and the edit only adds a warning log and carries on, which is `improved` and not a nudge, but the monitor still swallows the failure and keeps ticking, so the concern stays in the code as tracked debt.

The per-source catch that logs the error and continues was already there before the edit and is kept; the job still reports success with sources left unpinned, so the log-and-continue concern remains in the changed scope though nothing new was added.
The new helper repeats the file's existing pattern of swallowing New Relic attribute failures, which is telemetry emission that cannot change authentication correctness.

The new helper is a display formatter that falls back to the tzdb abbreviation when `Intl` has no name for the zone, a documented alternative source rather than a hidden failure of anything that matters.

The new catch only covers `Intl.DisplayNames` for an invalid region code and falls back to showing the ISO code as the country name, so the label degrades visibly and no required operation failure is hidden.
A doc and optionality change on an interface field only; no code path catches, converts or ignores a failure.
The edit adds one re-export and changes no behavior; there is no failure path in the diff.
Only a type union and its doc are widened; no runtime error handling changed.
The edit changes how a composite conflict key is built; there is no catch, fallback operator or failure value in the changed lines.

The catches are the same as before (request failure yields no redirect, unparsable URL is returned as-is) and the new `//` check returns null as a deliberate safety guard, not as a substitute for a failure.
The rewrite keeps throwing ForbiddenError for blocked paths and adds no catch or fallback value anywhere in the changed code.
This is test setup code, which the rule excludes; the added catch is also a probe that only decides whether a lock file is stale.
The edit drops `async` from an in-memory key-value API; every value check and thrown error is unchanged and no failure becomes silent.
The added updateMany and deleteMany only add access validation that throws; the mention loop keeps its pre-existing catch that logs a forbidden recipient and rethrows everything else.
